territorial_scope.description: Applies across France; the responsible digital strategy duty applies to communes and intercommunal bodies above 50,000 inhabitants (Art. 35).

evidence.quote: La présente loi sera exécutée comme loi de l'Etat.

summary.short: Sets measures to reduce the environmental footprint of digital use in France: bans on techniques restricting consumers' software installation, software-update duties on sellers, eco-design criteria and indicators for telecom operators, data-centre tax-relief conditions, public purchasing and reuse of IT equipment, and local strategies for large communes.
summary.long: Law no. 2021-1485 of 15 November 2021 seeks to reduce the environmental footprint of digital technology in France, in five chapters. Chapter I raises user awareness through education content and an observatory of digital environmental impacts and of AI's contribution to the ecological transition. Chapter II limits device renewal: it bans techniques, including software, that prevent installing chosen software after the period set by Consumer Code Art. L. 217-12, unless needed for conformity; it sets seller duties on software updates; and it adds reuse, repair and public-purchasing rules for IT equipment. Chapter III covers electronic communications and digital services: caller-identity rules for automated calls, eco-design criteria for digital services from 1 January 2024, and an audiovisual recommendation on energy information. Chapter IV covers data centres and networks: heat-recovery and water-use criteria for a data-centre tax incentive, operator environmental indicators, and mast-sharing rules. Chapter V sets local strategies: regional climate plans must address data-centre heat recovery, and communes and intercommunal bodies above 50,000 inhabitants must adopt a responsible digital strategy by 1 January 2025. Government reports are also required.

entities.function: Analyses and quantifies the direct and indirect environmental impacts of digital technology and the contribution of digital technology, including artificial intelligence, to the ecological transition; defines digital sobriety; publishes its work (Art. 4).

notes: Annotated from the text as promulgated (JORF 16 November 2021), not from consolidated codes; the code amendments are recorded as relations, not as consolidated text. target_instrument_id is an empty string where the target is not in the registry (the schema requires a string; codebook 3.8 says null). Art 29 requires a decree to set the turnover threshold below which operators are exempt, and Art 28 requires decree-set indicators; these delegated values are not coded here. Arts 27 and 36 are reports only. The text states no legal basis, sanctions or enforcement. enforcement.note: The text contains no fines, criminal penalties, licence revocation, benefit clawback, suspension or blocking provisions. Article 8 inserts a prohibition (new Art. L. 441-6 Code de la consommation) without a sanction, and Article 24 adds a power to prohibit and interrupt calls without a sanction. Penalties for these may exist in other codes, but this text does not state them.
